content: Ankle pain is a common issue that can arise as a result of either chronic or acute injuries, as well as degenerative diseases. Among the most frequent causes of ankle pain are ankle sprains, which typically occur due to a traumatic inversion injury. It is important to note that bilateral ankle swelling may suggest systemic causes, such as cardiac or vascular conditions, rather than localized foot or ankle pathology. Differential Diagnosis The potential causes of ankle pain include: Avulsion fractures of the distal fibula. Bimalleolar fractures. Degenerative joint disease. Diabetic arthropathy, also known as Charcot's arthropathy. Inversion sprains. Injuries involving inversion or eversion of the subtalar joint. Neoplasms. Entrapment of the peroneal nerve. Poor shoe alignment contributing to biomechanical stress. Repetitive injuries leading to disruption of the ankle retinaculum. Syndesmosis injuries. Trimalleolar fractures. Physical Examination A thorough physical examination should be conducted, including an assessment of the ankle, foot, and lower leg. Key components of the examination include: Evaluation of pulses to assess vascular integrity. Assessment of neurovascular status. Observation of skin color and capillary refill to evaluate perfusion. Imaging Studies X-rays: The Ottawa ankle rules can help determine the necessity of obtaining ankle X-rays following trauma. Indications for imaging include: Tenderness at the proximal fifth metatarsal. Tenderness along the distal 6 cm of the fibula or tibia. Tenderness in the navicular area. Inability to bear weight for at least four steps. If indicated, lateral X-rays, three-view ankle X-rays, stress views, foot series, or lower leg series may be performed. Normal imaging examples include lateral, oblique, and anteroposterior (AP) views of the ankle. MRI and CT: Advanced imaging modalities such as MRI or CT scans should be utilized if clinically indicated to further evaluate soft tissue or complex bony injuries. Other Diagnostic Studies Anterior and posterior drawer tests can be performed to assess ligamentous stability. Range of motion and muscle strength testing should be conducted to evaluate functional limitations. Treatment Treatment strategies for ankle pain and swelling can be guided by specific mnemonics to ensure comprehensive management.
